en: Farmers in the Banaue Rice Terraces use the inclined plane simple machine to move heavy loads up steep mountain paths.
The gravity on Mount Everest is slightly weaker than at sea level because you are farther from Earth's center.
The Maglev train in Japan uses powerful electromagnets to levitate above the tracks, eliminating friction for ultra-fast travel.
Alessandro Volta invented the first electrical battery, called the voltaic pile, in 1800 using alternating discs of zinc and copper.
Geckos can climb smooth glass walls because microscopic hairs on their toes increase friction and stick to the surface.
Bats navigate in the dark using echolocation, which relies on sound waves bouncing off objects to create a mental map.
The Tiwi Power Plant in Albay generates electricity by harnessing geothermal heat from hot underground rocks and steam.
The trans-Pacific fiber optic cable uses total internal reflection to transmit internet data as pulses of light underwater.
The Ekstraordinary roller coaster at Enchanted Kingdom converts gravitational potential energy into kinetic energy as it drops down steep hills.
The Catatumbo lightning in Venezuela produces up to 280 electrical strikes per hour due to unique wind and mountain conditions.
The Stanley Classic vacuum bottle keeps liquids hot by using a vacuum layer between its walls to prevent heat conduction.
Alexander Graham Bell invented the photophone in 1880, which transmitted sound on a beam of sunlight.
